readings: Using budget lines matched to their events (lines without a matching event left out), work out each event name's average budgeted `amount`, ignoring missing amounts. Find the event names whose average is above the average of the per-event-name averages, with each name counting once. For each one, show the event name, its average budgeted amount, how far that is above the average of the per-event-name averages, and its average as a ratio to the mean of these averages. No rounding.
queries:
WITH per_name AS (
    SELECT e.event_name AS event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS avg_amount
    FROM budget b
    JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    GROUP BY e.event_name
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS mean_avg FROM per_name
)
SELECT p.event_name,
       p.avg_amount,
       p.avg_amount - o.mean_avg AS diff_above_mean,
       p.avg_amount / o.mean_avg AS ratio_to_mean
FROM per_name p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE p.avg_amount > o.mean_avg;
